textBlocks.text: All questions are for both separate science and combined science students
1 The diagram shows the apparatus a student uses to separate a mixture of salt and sand. She adds the mixture to water in a beaker and then carries out the three stages shown.
(a) Give the names of the pieces of apparatus labelled X and Y.
(b) (i) A liquid that dissolves substances is a
(ii) The clear liquid that forms in stage 1 is a
(c) (i) At which stage, 1, 2 or 3, is the sand collected?
(ii) At which stage, 1, 2 or 3, is the salt collected?
(d) What happens to the water in stage 3?
2 A student investigates some food colourings, each of which is made up of one or more dyes.
She produces a chromatogram using the safe colourings red (SR), blue (SB) and green (SG) and food colourings red (FR), blue (FB) and green (FG).
SR SB SG FR FB FG
(a) How many dyes are there in SR?
(b) Complete the table by placing ticks ( ) next to the two food colourings that are definitely safe to use.
3 The box shows some methods that can be used in separating mixtures.
From the box, select the best method for each of the separations. You may use each method once, more than once or not at all.
(a) Removing sand from a mixture of sand and water.
(b) Obtaining pure water from a salt solution.
(c) Extracting the red dye from a sample of rose petals.
(d) Separating the coloured dyes in a sample of green ink.
(e) Obtaining ethanol (alcohol) from a mixture of ethanol and water.
4 (a) The list shows some techniques used to separate mixtures. crystallisation filtration fractional distillation paper chromatography simple distillation
Complete the table to show the best method of obtaining each substance from the mixture.
In each case, choose one of the letters A, B, C, D or E. Each letter may be used once, more than once or not at all.

(b) Gold occurs in ores, which are mixtures of gold and other substances. Several elements and compounds are used in the extraction of gold from its ores. Each box below represents the substances present in one part of the extraction process. Classify the contents of each box as a compound, an element or a mixture by writing your choice below each box.
5 The table shows the names of some common pieces of laboratory apparatus used to make measurements.
(a) Complete the table to show the name of the quantity that can be measured by each piece of apparatus, and a common unit used for that quantity. One example of each has been done for you.
(b) Which piece of apparatus is needed to make measurements in a paper chromatography experiment?
D stop clock (Total for Question 5 = 7 marks)
6 A student produces this chromatogram for four dyes, A, B, C and D.
(b) Each dye is made from one or more of the colours blue, red and yellow. The student thinks that the result for one dye is incorrect.
Suggest which result is incorrect. Explain your answer.
